column3: Correcting the Mythos of KL-Regularization: Direct Alignment without Overoptimization via Chi-Squared Preference Optimization (chi^2PO)
column7: NOT CITED. Related work para 3 (lines 697-706); Conclusion line 558 ('We do not claim that KL is preferable under every objective'); optionally Intro line 043.
column8: chi^2 (mixed with KL) regularization gives single-policy-concentrability guarantees against over-optimization, but only in the bandit/response-level setting; the natural 'why not chi^2?' objection to our KL-uniqueness claim.
column9: Their coverage coefficient is trajectory-level chi^2 (their App. D), so their guarantee never touches the multi-step inner term; say this explicitly.

column3: f-Divergence Regularized RLHF: Two Tales of Sampling and Unified Analyses
column7: Intro lines 039-043 (f-divergence generalizations); Related work para 3, right after Wang et al. (2024) at lines 699-700.
column8: Online RLHF with general f-divergence regularization gets O(log T) regret / O(1/T) gap via two sampling schemes; the on-policy side of general-f regularization.
column9: their guarantees use sampling from the current policy, which is exactly what off-policy permissibility rules out for every f except reverse KL.

column3: Better Estimation of the Kullback-Leibler Divergence Between Language Models
column7: Sec. 4 'Switching the estimator on and off' lines 475-483 and Fig. 7 (exact full-vocabulary arm); App. C.1 lines 1052-1056 ('exact regime available only when |A| is small'); App. D.16 vocabulary scaling.
column8: A Rao-Blackwellized KL estimator (exact next-token summation instead of a single sampled token) has provably lower variance and stabilizes RLHF training. They use the whole vocab |A| at every position (token)
column9: Their RB estimator is literally the "exact inner term" of Fig. 7 at token level, so in our App. C.1's "available only when |A| is small" should be softened.

column8: Deterministic integration over the top-k tokens tracks the exact Rao-Blackwellized KL with near-zero variance at low memory, with importance weights for off-policy use.

column3: On the Design of KL-Regularized Policy Gradient Algorithms for LLM Reasoning (RPG)
column7: Sec. 3.3 lines 343-352 (Schulman low-variance estimator, importance weighting); Intro lines 044-049 (off-policy compromises); Related work para 1 lines 679-687.
column8: Unified derivation of forward/reverse, normalized/unnormalized KL regularizers with correct gradient estimators and clipped importance-sampling variants for off-policy LLM RL. Overall, an interesintg paper.
column9: Shows the estimator-design question we raise for general Omega is live even for KL itself in on-policy RL.

column3: Rethinking KL Regularization in RLHF: From Value Estimation to Gradient Optimization
column7: Sec. 3.3 lines 343-352; Sec. 4 lines 475-483 (three estimator arms).
column8: k1/k2/k3 KL estimators used as losses vs. rewards: 'k3 as loss' (GRPO) is a biased first-order approximation with a chi^2-like heavy tail; gives principled off-policy corrections.
column9: Their heavy-tail finding for k3 is the same 1/u mechanism as our Fig. 6-7, seen from the KL-only side.

column3: KL-Regularized RLHF with Multiple Reference Models: Exact Solutions and Sample Complexity
column7: Related work para 1, lines 684-686 (after Vieillard et al. 2020 on why KL has strong guarantees).
column8: First exact solution and sample-complexity analysis for reverse-KL RLHF with several reference models, extended to forward KL.
column9: Recent KL-theory anchor; also a clean reverse-vs-forward-KL contrast to cite alongside our forward-KL results.

column3: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards (iStar)
column7: Sec. 2 lines 171-178 (bandit DPO transplanted to MDP); Related work para 3 lines 700-703 (next to Cho et al. / Kim et al.); Conclusion lines 557-563 (multi-turn direction).
column8: A multi-turn DPO objective derived from a multi-step MDP (not a bandit) yields step-wise implicit rewards from trajectory preferences, used as an implicit PRM for agentic RL.
column9: Published example of exactly the multi-step implicit-reward setting where our inner term appears; they use reverse KL, so our theorem explains why it works off-policy.

column3: Autoregressive Direct Preference Optimization (ADPO)
column7: Sec. 2 lines 171-178; Related work para 3 lines 697-706.
column8: Introduces the autoregressive (token-level) assumption before the Bradley-Terry model, separating token length from feedback length, and derives a token-level DPO loss.
column9: Same bandit-vs-token-MDP distinction we draw at lines 171-178; cite as a 2026 published instance. Discussed in Slack

column3: Is On-Policy Data always the Best Choice for Direct Preference Optimization-based LM Alignment?
column7: Intro lines 044-051 (off-policy premise); App. C.5 lines 1227-1230 (on- vs off-policy preference data).
column8: On-policy preference data is not uniformly better; alignment proceeds in stages where diverse off-policy data helps early and high-quality data later.
column9: Supports the premise that off-policy preference data is used deliberately, not only for compute reasons.

column3: Loss Functions and Operators Generated by f-Divergences
column7: Intro lines 039-043; Related work para 2 lines 689-695 (Legendre-Fenchel dual, closed-form soft policy).
column8: f-divergences generate convex losses and 'f-softargmax' operators that generalize the logistic loss and softmax through Fenchel duality.
column9: Cleanest modern reference for the Fenchel-dual soft-policy machinery in Sec. 2 / Lemma 1.

column3: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment
column7: Related work para 3 lines 697-706 (optional, with chi^2PO).
column8: Coverage (chi^2-type) governs inference-time alignment; pessimistic rejection sampling avoids the reward hacking that Best-of-N suffers as N grows.
column9: Optional companion to chi^2PO; cite only if you discuss coverage/pessimism.

column3: Future-KL Regularized GRPO: Process-Level Credit Assignment from f-Divergence Regularization (FRPO)
column7: Related work para 2 lines 689-695 (f-divergence regularization inside an MDP); Intro lines 039-043.
column8: The on-policy gradient of a token-wise f-divergence-regularized objective contains a 'future-KL' return-to-go term that local per-token KL losses omit; adding it improves reasoning RL.
column9: Their future-regularization term is the on-policy counterpart of our next-state inner term; worth one sentence of contrast (they sample, we cannot).

column3: On a few pitfalls in KL divergence gradient estimation for RL
column7: Sec. 3.3 lines 343-352.
column8: Differentiating through a KL estimate as a loss gives the wrong gradient, and ignoring the sequential structure gives only a partial gradient; shows the correct implementation.
column9: Short, widely read; pairs with Liu et al. (ICLR 2026) and Shah et al.

column3: A Comedy of Estimators: On KL Regularization in RL Training of LLMs
column7: Sec. 3.3 lines 343-352; Sec. 4 lines 475-483.
column8: KL-estimator configurations with biased gradients cause training instabilities; unbiased configurations generalize better in- and out-of-domain.
column9: Empirical backing for 'estimator choice, not divergence choice, is what practitioners actually vary'.

column3: Provably avoiding over-optimization in Direct Preference Optimization without knowing the data distribution (PEPO)
column7: Related work para 3 lines 697-706 (with chi^2PO).
column8: Pessimism via an ensemble of DPO policies on disjoint data subsets; single-policy concentrability without knowing the data distribution or fitting a reward model.
column9: Shows the 2026 pessimism line stays bandit-level; supports the 'collision' framing for the multi-step follow-up.

column3: Direct Preference Optimization with Rating Information: Practical Algorithms and Provable Gains (RDPO)
column7: Related work para 3 lines 697-706 (optional).
column8: Uses rating-gap information plus chi^2 regularization for faster statistical rates and single-policy concentrability.
column9: Optional; but from well-known authors

column3: TokenRatio: Principled Token-Level Preference Optimization via Ratio Matching (TBPO)
column7: Intro lines 039-043 (Bregman); Related work para 2 lines 689-695.
column8: Token-level Bregman density-ratio matching that generalizes the logistic/DPO loss while keeping training simple.
column9: Bregman-at-token-level instance; cite only if the Bregman line is expanded.

column3: Policy Mirror Descent for Regularized Reinforcement Learning: A Generalized Framework with Linear Convergence (GPMD)
column7: Related work para 2 lines 689-695 (after Tomar et al. 2022 mirror-descent policy optimization).
column8: Generalized policy mirror descent that picks the Bregman divergence to match the convex regularizer, with linear convergence for general regularizers.
